SYNTHETIC / FAKE TEST DOCUMENT — NOT A REAL PATIENT — FOR SOFTWARE TESTING ONLY
Riverbend Test Rheumatology Clinic (FAKE)
42 Placeholder Lane, Testville ON  Z9Z 9Z9 · Tel 555-0170 · Fax 555-0171

November 4, 2026

Dr. Henrietta Fakeham (FAKE)
Maple Test Family Health Team

Re: Jordan FAKE-Rivers · DOB: 3 March 1979 · Health card: 9999990117 (FAKE)

Dear Dr. Fakeham,

Thank you for asking me to see Jordan FAKE-Rivers, a 47-year-old teacher, about painful, swollen hands. I saw them in clinic today.

History
For about five months they have had pain and swelling in the small joints of both hands and both wrists, with morning stiffness lasting about two hours. Climbing stairs is now hard because both knees are sore. They have had no rash, no mouth ulcers, no dry eyes and no change in bowel habit. Their mother has hypothyroidism. They do not smoke and drink alcohol rarely, about two drinks a month.

Examination
Weight 71 kg. Eight swollen joints: the second and third knuckles of both hands, both wrists and the right knee. Twelve tender joints in total. Skin, nails, heart and lungs were normal.

Investigations
Blood tests on 28 October 2026: rheumatoid factor 64 IU/mL (normal below 14), anti-CCP antibodies 212 U/mL (normal below 20), CRP 18 mg/L, ESR 34 mm/h. Hemoglobin 124 g/L, ALT 22 U/L, creatinine 71 µmol/L. Hepatitis B and C tests were negative, and the chest X-ray was clear.
Hand X-rays show early erosions at the right second knuckle.

Impression
Seropositive rheumatoid arthritis with high disease activity and early erosions.

Plan
1. Methotrexate 15 mg by mouth once a week, on the same day each week, increasing to 20 mg weekly after 4 weeks if blood tests are fine.
2. Folic acid 5 mg by mouth once a week, taken the day after the methotrexate.
3. Prednisone 10 mg daily for 2 weeks, then 5 mg daily for 2 weeks, then stop.
4. Naproxen may continue for now at 500 mg twice daily with food; we will try to stop it once the methotrexate works.
5. I have sent a referral to the clinic's physiotherapist and occupational therapist.

I went through the following with Jordan before they left, and gave them a printed sheet. Methotrexate is taken once a week, never daily. They should not drink alcohol while on it, and must not get pregnant or father a child while on it and for 3 months after stopping. They should have blood tests (CBC, ALT, creatinine) every 2 weeks for the first 2 months, then monthly, and call the clinic at once if they get a fever, a cough with shortness of breath, or mouth sores. They will be seen again here in 6 weeks, in mid-December 2026.

Sincerely,

Dr. Priya FAKE-Okonjo, MD, FRCPC (FAKE)
Rheumatology, Riverbend Test Rheumatology Clinic

cc: Jordan FAKE-Rivers (patient copy)
